headline: Water Taxi and Charter Reservations in Kachemak Bay
reservation: While the town of Homer is open-access, wilderness activities across Kachemak Bay State Park require pre-arranged water taxis. Charter fishing and peak-season glamping on the Spit often sell out six months in advance; verify all state park fees and vessel safety certifications through official Alaska Department of Fish and Game or State Park channels.

days.title: The Spit and Sky Views

stops.name: Homer Spit
stops.detail: Walk the four-mile gravel bar to observe the boat harbor, local art galleries, and the ‘End of the Road’ atmosphere.

stops.name: Skyline Drive
stops.detail: Drive the ridge above town for a panoramic view of Kachemak Bay, the Spit, and distant glaciers.

days.driving: Allow 40 minutes; local transfers on the Spit are brief but can be congested
days.note: Parking on the Spit is limited during the summer halibut fishing peak.

days.title: Wilderness Across the Bay

stops.name: Grewingk Glacier Lake
stops.detail: Take a water taxi to the Glacier Spit trailhead for a hike toward the iceberg-filled lake at the foot of the glacier.

stops.name: Gull Island
stops.detail: Observe thousands of nesting seabirds from a marine tour boat on the return trip to the harbor.

days.driving: Walking and local water taxi only; transit times vary by sea state
days.note: Bear safety protocols are essential in the state park; pack out all trash and food.

days.title: Coastal Culture and Tides

stops.name: Islands and Ocean Visitor Center
stops.detail: Learn about the Alaska Maritime National Wildlife Refuge through interactive exhibits and naturalist programs.

stops.name: Bishop’s Beach
stops.detail: Explore tide pools at low tide and walk the shoreline beneath the dramatic bluffs west of town.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes total; town roads are well-maintained
days.note: Check local tide tables before visiting Bishop’s Beach to ensure safe access to pools.

days.title: Isolated Boardwalks
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Seldovia Ferry Terminal

stops.name: Seldovia
stops.detail: Take a ferry or bush plane to this remote village to walk the historic boardwalks and visit the Russian Orthodox church.

stops.name: Otter Beach
stops.detail: A quiet spot in Seldovia for beachcombing and views of the Cook Inlet volcanoes.

days.driving: Ferry or flight transfer; allow full day for round trip
days.note: Check ferry schedules carefully as services may be limited outside of peak summer.

intel.title: Harbor Area Congestion
intel.text: The Homer Spit can become extremely crowded in July. Use the designated long-term parking lots if you are heading out on a full-day fishing charter.

intel.title: Remote Areas
intel.text: Signal is generally strong in Homer but disappears completely once you cross the bay into Kachemak Bay State Park. Coordinate water taxi pickups clearly before leaving the harbor.

intel.title: Mainland Supply
intel.text: Fuel and full-service groceries are available in the main town area of Homer. Prices typically reflect the remote coastal location.

intel.title: Tidal Shifts
intel.text: Homer experiences some of the world's largest tidal ranges. Do not leave vehicles parked on beach flats and monitor water levels during shoreline walks.

intel.title: Water Taxis
intel.text: Access to the most famous glacier hikes is by boat only. These operations are weather-dependent; have a town-based alternative ready if seas are too high.

plan.arrival: Landing at HOM, a rental car is recommended for exploring Skyline Drive and the bluffs; check in to your Spit or hillside lodging before dinner.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are fine for town; RVs are popular on the Spit but require advanced site reservations.
plan.goldenHour: Skyline Drive offers the premier sunset vantage point over the bay, subject to coastal cloud cover.
